title: Emit stage identifiers in metrics and traces for Dedicated pool staged rollouts
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Motivation: Staged rollouts for Dedicated pools need stage-scoped signals (latency/error/saturation/OOM) so the policy engine can evaluate gates deterministically and the Console can show evidence per stage. Today most metrics/traces are only tagged with pool_id/model/version/region, which makes it hard to attribute regressions to the canary partition vs baseline. This PR adds stage identifiers to a small set of request-scoped metrics and spans, with explicit cardinality controls (allowlist + value constraints) to avoid a repeat of high-cardinality label explosions. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce `rollout_stage_id` + `rollout_stage_idx` tags in the request context (propagated from router -> dataplane -> metrics/tracing). (2) Emit stage tags on key SLO/gate metrics only (request duration buckets, request error counters, 429/drop counters, queue depth, OOM counters), leaving the rest unchanged. (3) Add an allowlist-based label filter in the telemetry emitter with hard caps on value length and a denylist for free-form fields. (4) Add sampling + aggregation guardrails for span tags (only tag root request span + a single child span; do not tag per-token spans). (5) Feature flag `dedicated_rollout_stage_telemetry_tags` to allow safe enablement per environment/account. Notes on cardinality: `rollout_stage_id` is a short stable identifier (<= 16 chars, base32) and `rollout_stage_idx` is an int string (0..N). We explicitly do NOT include stage name, plan name, or arbitrary customer metadata. For multi-region pools, region remains a separate tag; stage_id is shared across regions for the same promotion step. Rollout stage tags are optional; when absent we emit no tag and do not substitute "unknown" to avoid creating a new high-cardinality value. Rollout/gates behavior: This PR does not change gate evaluation logic; it only emits the signals needed by ENG-5941/ENG-5941 follow-ups and the dashboards in observability-pack. Testing: unit tests for label allowlist/filtering, integration test that stage context from routing attaches to metrics, and a soak test config that validates the top-N time series count does not change materially when the flag is off. Rollout plan: land behind flag; enable in staging for 48h; then enable for beta Dedicated accounts only. If we see increased series churn, we can disable the flag with no config migration.
commits: telemetry: add rollout stage tags to request context and span attributes
metrics: allowlist + value guards for stage tags; denylist free-form labels
routing/dedicated: propagate stage metadata through router -> backend headers
tests: label filter unit tests + stage propagation integration test
docs: telemetry tag policy update for staged rollouts

review_conversation: Allison Grant (comment): Please confirm we are not tagging per-token metrics/spans with stage_id; that would blow up our series count and trace payload size. Also, please document the label allowlist policy (what gets tagged and why). Caleb Johnson (reply): Confirmed: only request-level SLO metrics + root request span are tagged; per-token metrics remain unchanged and per-token spans do not get the stage attributes. Added explicit tests and a note in docs/observability/metrics-labeling-policy.md. Logan Wright (comment): The label filter needs to be centralized; right now we have a filter in metrics emitter but not in tracing. We should enforce the same constraints (max length, allowed keys) across both so future tags can't sneak in. Caleb Johnson (reply): Agreed; added `label_policy.go` and reused in tracing span tag helper. Both metrics and tracing now share allowlist/denylist and the value length cap. Sergio Costa (comment): For dashboards, can we also emit stage_idx? It's useful for ordered stage panels even when stage_id is opaque. Caleb Johnson (reply): Added `rollout_stage_idx` tag (stringified int) alongside stage_id; still optional. Mina Haddad (comment): Header propagation from router to dataplane: please ensure this cannot be spoofed by end users hitting the pool endpoint directly. Also should be stripped on external ingress. Caleb Johnson (reply): Updated middleware to only accept stage headers from internal trusted hops (mTLS service identity + internal network). External ingress strips `x-redwood-rollout-*` headers. Jordan Lee (comment): When stage metadata is missing, we should fail closed or mark it unknown? From a policy perspective, missing data handling matters. Caleb Johnson (reply): This PR intentionally emits nothing when absent; policy engine will handle missing stage tags (likely treat as insufficient evidence). Adding "unknown" would create a new time series and make dashboards noisier; aligned with SRE guidance in thread 1738976011. Requested changes: (1) add feature flag and default OFF in prod; (2) ensure stage_id length cap; (3) add series-budget CI check. Addressed in follow-up commits. Approvals: Logan Wright ✅; Allison Grant ✅; Sergio Costa ✅; Mina Haddad ✅; Jordan Lee ✅.
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds optional `rollout_stage_id` / `rollout_stage_idx` tags to a limited set of request metrics and tracing spans to support Dedicated staged rollout gate attribution. Guarded by `dedicated_rollout_stage_telemetry_tags` feature flag; includes label allowlist and anti-cardinality protections.
